title: Perfect tests suffice for pseudo-coherent tensor tests on algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for the objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Derived tensor uses K-flat resolutions and $R\Gamma$ uses K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. A perfect object is etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Pseudo-coherent on a space means that etale locally on affine scheme charts the object is represented by a bounded-above complex of finite free structure modules; pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ means quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above finite-free $A$-complex [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Quasi-compact means every open cover of the point space has a finite subcover, and quasi-separated means the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and suppose $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all $i>b$, for some integer $b$. If $R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every perfect $P$, then $R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ is pseudo-coherent in $D(A)$ for every pseudo-coherent $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$.

proof.text: Put $f:X\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$. The affine-scheme qcqs lemma and space qcqs-permanence imply that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $f$ is qcqs. Apply the affine-chart uniform vanishing statement with $V=Y$ and $W=X$: there is $N\ge1$ with $R^p\Gamma(X,M)=0$ for every quasi-coherent $M$ and $p\ge N$. The enlarged-site equivalence identifies its $F_Y$ with global sections: $X$ is terminal in the enlarged site, and its equalizer formula computes global sections on the small site. Global sections are left exact and preserve countable products, since $\Gamma=\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_X,-)$ and a map into a product is a tuple of maps. The product-preserving-derived-functor bound therefore gives $H^i(R\Gamma(X,L))=0$ for $i\ge t+N$ if $L\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$ has $H^q(L)=0$ for $q>t$. This also holds for $A$-module-valued derived sections: applying global sections to the same K-injective module-sheaf representative gives the same underlying abelian-group complex, and an $A$-module with zero underlying group is zero.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, proof first paragraph; Tag 08FA, proof (2), using the affine-chart case of Tag 08F7(3).

proof.text: Fix any pseudo-coherent $E$ and any $m\in\mathbf Z$, and set $a=m-N-1-b$. The space perfect-approximation theorem gives a distinguished triangle $P\xrightarrow{u}E\to C\to P[1]$ with $P$ perfect and all three terms in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, with $H^i(u)$ an isomorphism for $i>a$ and $H^a(u)$ surjective. Only qcqs is needed; in particular no scheme representability or Noetherian hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, perfect approximation of (X,E,m-N-1-b) by Tag 08HP.

proof.text: For $i\ge a$ the exact row $H^i(P)\to H^i(E)\to H^i(C)\to H^{i+1}(P)\to H^{i+1}(E)$ has its first map surjective and its last map injective. Exactness forces $H^i(C)=0$. This includes $i=a$, where only surjectivity, not injectivity, of $H^a(u)$ was assumed. Thus $C$ has cohomology zero above $a-1$.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, cone cohomology vanishes in degrees at least m-N-1-b.

proof.text: Use the standard truncation description to represent $C$ by a complex zero above $a-1$ and $K$ by one zero above $b$. The bounded-above flat replacement statement, applied on the small ringed etale site, gives flat-term complexes with the same respective upper term bounds. They are K-flat by the site version of bounded-above flat K-flatness, and the site-derived-tensor model computes $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K$ by their total tensor. In degree $j>a-1+b$, each summand $F^r\otimes G^s$ with $r+s=j$ is zero: nonzero summands would require both $r\le a-1$ and $s\le b$. Hence $H^j(C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)=0$ for $j\ge a+b=m-N-1$.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, tensor upper bound; sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat and lemma-K-flat-resolution.

proof.text: The algebraic-space derived tensor closure statement applies because $C$ and $K$ have quasi-coherent cohomology. Thus $C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$. Apply step 1 with $t=m-N-2$, using step 4. It gives $H^i(R\Gamma(X,C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K))=0$ for $i\ge m-2$, in particular for $i\ge m-1$. The extra degree of slack comes from choosing $N\ge1$ with the vanishing convention $p\ge N$; it only strengthens the bound needed here.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, bound on derived sections of the tensor cone; Tag 08F5 for quasi-coherence.

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative of $K$ using the site-derived-tensor equivalence. The fixed-K-flat-tensor exactness statement takes the triangle of step 2 to a distinguished triangle. The K-injective right-derived-functor statement then gives a distinguished triangle in $D(A)$ with terms $T_P=R\Gamma(X,P\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$, $T_E=R\Gamma(X,E\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$ and $T_C=R\Gamma(X,C\otimes^{\mathbf L}K)$. In the cohomology exact sequence, $H^{i-1}(T_C)=H^i(T_C)=0$ for every $i\ge m$ by step 5. Therefore $H^i(T_P)\to H^i(T_E)$ is an isomorphism for all $i\ge m$.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, high-degree comparison of tensor global sections, including both adjacent cone groups.

proof.text: The perfect-test hypothesis makes $T_P$ pseudo-coherent. The ring all-m criterion gives a bounded finite-free complex $F$ and a map $F\to T_P$ inducing isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection at $m$. Compose with $T_P\to T_E$. By step 6 the composite still induces isomorphisms above $m$ and a surjection at $m$, so it witnesses that $T_E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent by definition. This holds for every integer $m$; the same ring criterion implies that $T_E$ is pseudo-coherent. Since $E$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion.

source.place: Tag 0CWH, final paragraph; more-algebra.tex Tag 064U, lemma-pseudo-coherent, and Tag 064Q, definition-pseudo-coherent.
